newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England signals no change in rates.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England signals no change in rates.

text.p: The Bank of England did not operate in the UK money market in the early round, implying no change in official interest rates from 6.0 percent after Wednesday's monetary meeting.
Any day-after adjustment in interest rates is normally signalled in the first round of operations and it would be unusual for the Bank to change rates in subsequent market operations.
Bank of England Governor Eddie George and Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke held their monthly monetary meeting on Wednesday morning.
"It is likely that if they had agreed to raise rates yesterday, they would have done it by now," said Ian Stewart, UK economist at Merrill Lynch.
"It's unlikely that they would wait until midday to act."

Clarke unexpectedly raised official rates by a quarter of a point to 6.0 percent on October 30 but the Bank of England has since said further rises would be needed to ward off a future upsurge in inflation.
Speaking in Lisbon on Wednesday night, George said the question of a rate increase needed to be addressed soon, but a rise need not be particularly steep.
